exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal, emergency cesarean section, elective cesarean section)
outcome: postnatal depression (measured by Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores)
cohort: The study included 267 women who delivered singleton fetuses and were assessed for postnatal depression 1 week after delivery at Jordan University Hospital.
finding: The study found no significant association between the mode of delivery and postnatal depression, but the occurrence of intrapartum complications was associated with an approximately two times greater risk of developing postnatal depression.
mod_finding: There was no significant association or difference in postnatal depression scores between different modes of delivery (vaginal, emergency cesarean section, elective cesarean section).
gest_age: The gestational age at the time of delivery showed no significant differences in postnatal depression scores.
